newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Market protection not answer to competition - ASX.
newsitem.headline: Market protection not answer to competition - ASX.

text.p: The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) said on Thursday that protection for stock markets from further competition was not the answer to the problem of market fragmentation.
"Stock markets are supposed to be the heart of the market economy," ASX managing director Richard Humphry said in a speech prepared for delivery to a Toronto seminar and issued here.
"It strikes me as rather incongruous for a stock exchange that operates such a market to try to isolate itself from competition, however worthy the ultimate objective may be," he said.

While fragmentation had undesirable consequences, including increased spreads and volatility and impaired price discovery, the real answer was to match the attractions of opposition markets, Humphries said.
"The only answer in our view is to beat the newcomers at their own game," he said.
"Fragmentation is the result of investor choice and wouldn't occur if investors chose to trade in one market," he said.
"But rational investors will only choose to move from the principal market to trade in the new market if the new market offers them advantages that exceed the disadvantages of less transparency."

In responding to institutional investor demands for greater anonymity, one of the attractions of proprietary trading systems, the ASX had introduced a weighted single price system at the end of each day to facilitate bloc trades, he said.

Humphry said ASX research indicated insufficient investor interest to justify new markets for smaller stocks in Australia, although demand for assistance in the earlier stages of capital raising was clear and the ASX was taking steps to meet that demand.
"What our research indicates there is a demand for is a better primary market for start-ups to facilitate their initial raising of capital," he said.
"We plan to meet this demand by creating a new primary market using Internet technology and both the Internet and more traditional distribution systems," Humphry said.
The new market to provide a structure so capital providers and users can meet and negotiate was to be called the Alternative Capital Market, he said.
